survivors.claim: The spec Behavior section requires a legacy BRIEF ratification to name every rejected candidate from the old design-pick.json (when that file exists) in the doctrines Dissents section, falling back to no-name-required only when design-pick.json is absent. The build deleted this fallback entirely instead.
survivors.impact: A legacy host whose old design-pick.json still records rejected design candidates with reasons can now ratify BRIEF without naming any of them in the doctrine Dissents section, losing the provenance guarantee the spec promises for legacy resumes.
survivors.evidence: Spec text says: Dissents check: legacy runs with no mocks status use the old design-pick.json rejected list when that file exists, else no name is required. The shipped code runs the composed-direction Dissents check only when the mark is not legacy and the archetype is visual -- for a legacy run it is skipped outright with no design-pick.json read anywhere in the file. The helper functions that used to read design-pick.json were removed entirely from the driver (confirmed by grepping spec and tests for the literal, which shows no remaining reference inside the driver script). The deviations sidecar documents this cut as forced by the retired-literal sweep AC, but no locked Decision authorizes dropping this specific Behavior fallback -- the one sanctioned build ruling covers only two unrelated retired-mark literals in the refusal table.
